skill.description: Use Flux 1 Kontext Pro through RunComfy to perform targeted edits on one source image. The skill documents prompts, CLI invocation, schema fields, and model selection guidance.

security_audit.summary: Most static shell findings are Markdown formatting false positives, not executable Ruby backticks. Confirmed risks are the intended RunComfy CLI execution, global CLI installation guidance, and third-party processing of prompts, image URLs, and outputs. No prompt-injection attempt or hidden exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before installing or running the RunComfy CLI, and show the exact command and destination service.
Warn users that prompts, image URLs, and generated outputs are processed by RunComfy. Avoid sensitive private images unless approved.
Document token revocation and prefer environment-scoped tokens in CI. Never print or store RUNCOMFY_TOKEN in prompts or logs.

content.user_title: Edit Images with Flux Kontext on RunComfy
content.value_statement: Precise image edits often drift when prompts are too broad or use the wrong model. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to use Flux 1 Kontext Pro through RunComfy for targeted single-image edits.
actual_capabilities: Routes explicit Flux Kontext image-edit requests to the RunComfy Model API workflow.
Shows the required prompt and image fields for the Flux 1 Kontext Pro edit endpoint.
Provides prompt patterns that preserve identity, pose, framing, brands, and lighting.
Includes command examples for local edits, seeded variants, and output directory selection.
Explains when to choose sibling tools for multi-image, text-heavy, or text-to-image tasks.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and network access.
Supports one source image per request.
Uses publicly fetchable HTTPS image URLs for inputs.
Does not guarantee perfect text edits or complex multi-change compositions.

use_cases.title: Refine a Product Photo
use_cases.description: A designer can replace label text or adjust one visible detail while preserving lighting and composition.

use_cases.title: Create Controlled Campaign Variants
use_cases.description: A marketer can create seeded versions of a hero image with one controlled visual change.

use_cases.title: Integrate Image Edits in Workflows
use_cases.description: A developer can call the RunComfy CLI from an approved environment and save generated assets to a chosen folder.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Local Edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Flux Kontext on this image URL: [image URL]. Keep the subject unchanged and add [single object or detail]. Save the result to [folder].

prompt_templates.title: Preserve Brand Assets
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit this product image with Flux Kontext: [image URL]. Keep the bottle, lighting, camera angle, and background unchanged. Replace only [old text] with [new text].

prompt_templates.title: Seeded Variant Series
prompt_templates.prompt: Run Flux Kontext for this source image: [image URL]. Use seed [number]. Keep all core elements unchanged and change only [one visual attribute].

prompt_templates.title: Model Selection Check
prompt_templates.prompt: I need an image edit with these inputs: [image count], [goal], [text requirements]. Decide whether Flux Kontext is the right RunComfy model, then run it only if it fits.

output_examples.input: User asks to add a red scarf to a portrait while keeping the face unchanged.
output_examples.output: The skill responds with a focused Flux Kontext edit instruction, notes the image URL requirement, and prepares a RunComfy CLI invocation.

output_examples.input: User wants to change product label text without changing lighting or camera angle.
output_examples.output: The skill prioritizes preservation wording, asks for an approved source image URL, and uses a seed if the user wants variants.

output_examples.input: User provides five reference images and asks for one combined edit.
output_examples.output: The skill explains that Flux Kontext is single-reference only and recommends a multi-image workflow instead.

best_practices: Use one clear edit instruction per request.
State what must remain unchanged before describing the desired change.
Use approved images and understand that inputs are processed by RunComfy.
anti_patterns: Combining several unrelated edits in one prompt.
Using Flux Kontext for multi-reference image editing.
Passing sensitive private images or secret text without explicit approval.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps an agent use Flux 1 Kontext Pro on RunComfy for targeted edits to one source image.

faq.question: Does it generate images from scratch?
faq.answer: No. It is for image-to-image edits. Use a text-to-image model when there is no source image.

faq.question: What tools do I need?
faq.answer: You need the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account or token, and network access.

faq.question: Can it edit several images at once?
faq.answer: No. It is designed around one input image. Use a multi-image workflow for batches.

faq.question: Where are my prompts and image URLs sent?
faq.answer: The RunComfy CLI sends them to the RunComfy Model API for processing.

faq.question: How should I prompt it?
faq.answer: Use a short declarative edit and clearly name the parts that must remain unchanged.
